cells.tense: You are here, pen in hand, watching the pattern come into focus.
cells.act: follow the pull of what might be felt, a little way
cells.ask: Take a conversation you keep replaying because something in it didn't sit right, and follow the feeling under it a little way — before you work out who was right. Nothing has to get settled.
cells.core:
You can read what's going on between people quickly — who gave what, who paid more, what really happened under what was said — and you don't let that come out as a verdict. You see the imbalance and you still leave room for the person beside you. The read doesn't have to rush the room.

The balance is held together by something you haven't looked at directly: what the situation made you feel. Let that come first tonight. One uneven moment you keep turning over — let the feeling under it be there before you work out who owed what. Nothing gets settled, and you get to feel what the whole thing has been costing you, which is information your reading of it has been skipping over.

cells.tense: You will have weighed next week long before next week gets here.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Pick an unfair situation you've been holding open and close it today, without laying out why. Don't wait until you're certain — decide what's fair and put it into effect.
cells.core:
You read a situation fast enough to see the imbalance before most people have noticed it, and the fast read is outrunning the situation itself. You know who is behind, who will be behind, and what it will cost, so the account is settled in your mind before anyone else sits down. The scale keeps working after it has all the information it needs.

That is what the steady hand is for: when the call is clear, close it and move. Tonight, take a situation you have been holding open and decide it in one motion — not perfectly, just done — and don't explain to anyone afterward. The room will find the floor steadier without the reasoning. And the thinking you didn't show anyone is where the balance gets to keep costing you less.

cells.tense: The imbalance between you and someone else is still sitting where you left it.
cells.act: walk toward what connects, leaving what does not
cells.ask: A relationship where the balance has been off — someone you've been keeping at a polite distance — take one step back toward them. Say a true thing you've been holding out of it.
cells.core:
The fairness you used to bring to close relationships has stopped coming out. That sharp read is still there in your head; it turns over old moments — what was said, who owed what — and doesn't reach a call. The imbalance you notice between you and someone else isn't weighed, and the door you're standing at has been shut behind you a while.

Something has to be let go of. Not your judgment — the distance. There's a person with whom things are uneven, and the step is small: a true thing, said once, without settling who was right. That move is yours to make. What comes after isn't yours to control, and that's the point. The room will recalibrate around a move, not around a thought.
cells.sheetLine: The step is small: a true thing, said once.

cells.tense: You are keeping things even between people, and your account says you stay out of it.
cells.act: gather the feelings that might be felt and look at them
cells.ask: At the next moment when you smooth something over, gather what you noticed and what you chose, and say it to someone as yours — not as the calm thing that happened.
cells.core:
What's going on between people is balanced around you because someone reads the room and adjusts the weight, a word here and a small correction there, and your own account of it has you staying out of the way. The scale is being worked. The worker tells it as a witness, while the people nearby have been watching you do it — they can tell when the balancing has already happened.

The smoothing you do looks like something that came from the room, and it came from you. Notice what you said or softened this week and don't call it nothing — gather what you felt first and what you decided after, and hold both. You don't have to announce it. Just let what you actually did stop going out of the balance and into the room's air.
cells.sheetLine: Someone balances the room, and the worker says it isn't them.

attempts.check: The kernel says a pattern has been recognized (a transient), but nothing supports what the person did with it or that they named it; the Too Much and Too Little cores say what the analysis costs them, which they can recognize from inside and reject, and the reads survive that because the asks stand on their own. The drafts I cut served me more than them: 'you see through things' and 'you're the clearest read in the room,' which flatter a gift the record only names, and 'nobody argues with your read,' which puts a claim in other people's mouths. The one place I overreached is Unacknowledged: I attributed the fair-looking of someone's own feelings to that person as the hidden source, which is fair reconstruction from the misattribution mechanism, but a person could reasonably say the opposite is true, so the core leans on what they can check — what gets said out loud, who corrects whom, when the evenness was set — and the ask holds even if the hidden-authorship reading is wrong, because looking at one's own feeling before it is compared to another's does not depend on whose authorship is being misread.
